newsitem.title: POLAND: ZLOTY EASES VS BASKET IN ACTIVE TRADE, DEPOS FLAT.
newsitem.headline: ZLOTY EASES VS BASKET IN ACTIVE TRADE, DEPOS FLAT.

text.p: The Polish zloty closed slightly weaker against the basket of currencies, after a day of busy trade caused by large dollar/mark swings and subsequent speculation on zloty crosses, dealers said.
They also said that after weeks of strong zloty buying on the back of good fundamentals many investors had now long zloty positions and slowed purchases making trade more balanced.
"Trade was really busy today, and the zloty moved along with dollar/mark swings with players taking full advantage of speculative possiblities," said Bogdan Stepkowski of ING bank.

The zloty closed at 2.44/2.39 percent from the trading band centre, weaker than Monday's 2.53/2.43 percent close. It closed at 3.1510/25 to the dollar, up from 3.1525/45 on Monday and at 1.8570/77 to the mark, down from 1.8515/35.

But dealers said it might rebound to 2.5 percent tomorrow on the so-called "Wednesday syndrome" as banks cut currency positions to keep higher yielding zloty instruments on accounts over the weekend, only to reverse deals on Thursday.
"The zloty should probe higher tomorrow because of the Wednesday syndrome," one dealer at a foreign bank here said. "It is likely to go up to 2.48 percent (from the parity rate)."
On the money market overnight and tomorrow/next rates held flat at around 22 percent underpinned by the National Bank of Poland's seven and 14-day reverse repo rates of 22.09 and 22.15 percent.
Dealers did not expect rates to change substantially tomorrow as much of the payments for T-bills bought on Monday would be offset by redemption inflows.
